container.layout: Every bar panel (audio, bluetooth, network, monitor, power, clock, weather, elsewhen, agents, tailscale, dropbox) is a KeyboardPanel, not a PopupCard. A KeyboardPanel is a full-screen, transparent wlr-layer-shell surface on the Overlay layer (namespace omarchy-keyboard-panel) on the widget's monitor. It draws one card inside itself and no scrim: everything outside the card stays fully visible. Top bar: the card's top edge is at y = barThickness + gap = 26 + 5 = 31, so a 5px strip of desktop shows between bar and card. The card is centred horizontally on the widget slot's centre: x = round(clamp(slotX + slotW/2 - W/2, 5, screenW - W - 5)). Panels on the right of the bar therefore pin to 5px from the screen's right edge. Example at 1440px: audio's slot spans 1351..1378, so the centre is 1364.5. A 380px card wants x = 1174.5, which clamps to 1440-380-5 = 1055, so the card spans 1055..1435. Card: an opaque popups.background fill, a 2px border in popups.border (the Hyprland active-border colour or gradient; flat accent in Tokyo Night) drawn inside the box, and square corners (radius = cornerRadius = 0). It has 14px padding inside the border, so content starts 16px in from each outer edge. W is the panel's contentWidth, the card's outer width: 380 for most panels, 560 clock, 480 weather, 340 elsewhen. H = content implicit height + 32, capped per panel and by the screen height - 36. Open: the card fades from 0 to 1 opacity and scales from 0.97 to 1 about the point on its top edge nearest the widget's centre. This takes 180ms on bezier (0.23, 1, 0.32, 1). Close takes 120ms on the same curve. Hyprland's layer animation is turned off for this namespace, so all motion is QML. Content that arrives after opening (a wifi scan, new BT devices) grows the card height over 200ms on the same curve, clipping the content while it grows. The height snaps during the first 60ms after opening. One panel per bar at a time. Opening another closes the current one. When both widgets are in the same bar section (the three centre sections count as one), the card morphs instead: x, y, w and h interpolate from the old card to the new one over 220ms ease-out, the new content fades in at opacity min(1, morph*1.6), and the old card fades out over it. Across sections the new card simply grows in. Dismissal: a click anywhere outside the card with any mouse button closes the panel, including clicks on other monitors (each gets a transparent catcher surface). Clicks on the bar strip (y <= 31) are forwarded to the bar widget under the pointer. Clicking the same widget toggles the panel closed; clicking another widget switches panels in one click. Esc closes the panel. Tab and Shift+Tab move to the next or previous panel in the same bar section. While the panel is open, the bar draws the accent open-panel pill under the widget (see bar.json openPanel.mark).

popupCard.layout: PopupCard is an xdg-popup parented to the bar window. Only the tray (the manage popup and the per-app menu) and the media widget use it. It is placed below the widget: y = widget bottom + margin = 26 + 5 = 31 from the bar's top, and x = widgetCentre - W/2, clamped 5px from the screen edges. PopupAdjustment.Slide lets the compositor slide it back on screen. Card: the same 2px popups border, popups.background, 14px padding and radius 0 as panels. Default size 280x200; callers pass fittedContentWidth/Height. Animation: opacity 0 to 1 and scale 0.97 to 1 about the card's top centre (Item.Top, not the icon point), 180ms in and 120ms out on Style.easeOut. There is no morph. Click-mode popups use a HyprlandFocusGrab: a click anywhere outside the popup and its bar closes it. Hover-mode popups are passive. They take part in the bar's one-popout-at-a-time rule.

controls.layout: Panels are built from a small kit in shell/Ui. Usage counts across the panel sources: PanelToolTip 25, PanelSeparator 23, PanelSectionHeader 22, PanelActionButton 13, TextField 12, CursorSurface 8, ToggleSwitch 6, PanelSlider 5, PanelHero 3, Button 3, ConfirmDialog 1 (agents). Dropdown, ButtonGroup and NumberField are not used by any panel. Typical rhythm: a PanelHero at the top (icon, 14px bold title, 10px uppercase meta line, optional trailing ToggleSwitch). Sections are separated by a 1px foreground@0.12 rule, each introduced by a 10px bold header in Qt.darker(foreground, 1.4). Rows are CursorSurface backgrounds, transparent at rest. Hover or the keyboard cursor paints foreground@0.08 with a 1px foreground@0.25 border. The current or selected row paints foreground@0.18 with no border. Mouse hover moves the panel's single keyboard cursor, so only one row is ever highlighted. Right-edge 23x23 icon buttons do inline actions; destructive ones tint red on hover. Sliders are a 4px track with a 14px round knob. Switches are a 42x22 track with a 16px knob, square-cornered at rounding 0. All corners follow cornerRadius (0), except the slider track, fill and knob, which are always fully rounded.

(2) Year rail, 6px below the hero block, as wide as the grid (426px) and centered: "2026" (bodySmall 11, letterSpacing 1, Qt.darker(fg,1.5)) at left, then a 6px track (fg alpha 0.12) with a solid fill of selectedStateColor (= foreground) at round(width*yearDone), 12px from each label, then "84%" (bodySmall 11, fg) at right. (4) Month grid, 18px below the rail, centered, 426px wide: a header row 16px tall [W heading 32px][14px gutter][7 weekday labels, 52px each, e.g. SUN MON TUE WED THU FRI SAT, caption 10 bold, letterSpacing 1, darker 1.5], 2px cell spacing; then always 6 week rows, 3px apart, each [ISO week number 32x34, caption 10, darker 1.9][14px gutter][7 day cells 52x34]. audio.layout: Bar widget: a single BarIconButton glyph (Font Awesome speaker set, or headphones) in the 27px icon slot; no tooltip. Panel card content is 380px wide (fittedContentWidth(380)) and fits its content height up to a 560px cap, beyond which a ScrollView scrolls (vertical bar only when overflowing). One Column, 14px between blocks. (1) Hero, ~34px tall (the ToggleSwitch, 54x34 incl. its 6px cursor pad, is the tallest piece): speaker glyph at display 24px in foreground on the left (opacity 0.5 when output muted); 14px gap; a two-line label column, 2px apart: 'Audio' (title 14px bold, foreground) over the volume mood name uppercased, e.g. 'STEADY GROOVE' (caption 10px bold, letterSpacing 1.2, Qt.darker(foreground,1.4)); a ToggleSwitch on the far right (checked = anything audible), the label column stops 12px short of it. (2) PanelSeparator (1px). (3) OUTPUT block, Column spacing 6: header row with PanelSectionHeader 'OUTPUT' on the left and the percent, e.g. '62%', on the right (caption 10px bold, Qt.darker(foreground,1.4), 6px right margin, opacity 0.5 when muted); then the output slider row, 30px tall (PanelSlider 22px + controlGap 8), slider inset 6px left/right, range 0-1 step 0.05; then one row per output device, ~28px each (text line + 10px): a 22px-wide centred device glyph at title 14px, 8px gap, device name at body 12px foreground, elided, bold when it is the default output; the default output row carries the selected fill (foreground alpha 0.18). (4) Separator + INPUT block (hidden when there is no default source and no source rows), Column spacing 6: header 'INPUT' with percent on the right ('–' when an untyped source's level is unknown); input slider row 40px (PanelSlider 22 + 5 gap + 5px live peak meter + controlGap 8; 30px with the slider alone, centred, when no meter); then one row per input device like the output rows with microphone/headset/bluetooth/camera glyphs. (5) Separator + per-app mixer (only when at least one playback stream exists), Column spacing 10: header 'SOURCES', then one ~52px row per stream: a line with a 22px clickable mute glyph (title 14px), the app name (body 12px, bold when it is the media service's active player) and a 36px right-aligned percent (caption 10px bold, Qt.darker(foreground,1.5)); 2px below, a full-width PanelSlider range 0-1.5 (up to 150%). Rows are inset 6px left/right inside their CursorSurface. The keyboard/mouse cursor paints a single hover-cursor fill (foreground alpha 0.08) and 1px border (alpha 0.25) on whichever row it is on. Typical content (2 outputs, 1 input with meter, 1 stream) is ~410px tall, so no scroll. Text heights here are font-metric estimates for JetBrainsMono Nerd Font; control heights are exact.

power.layout: Bar widget: battery glyph in the 27px icon slot; with the showPercentage setting on (right-click toggles it) the slot doubles to 54px and a percent label, e.g. '87%', is drawn to the LEFT of the glyph with 4px gap. No tooltip. The widget is invisible and 0-sized when UPower reports no battery, and the panel refuses to open. Panel card content is 380px wide; height fits its content with no cap. One Column, 14px gaps. (1) Hero ~37px tall (the 28px bold percent sets the height): battery glyph at display 24px foreground on the left; 14px gap; label column (2px line gap) with 'Battery' (title 14px bold foreground) over the status line uppercased (caption 10px bold, letterSpacing 1.2, Qt.darker(foreground,1.4)), e.g. 'SLURPING POWER' rotating every 2.8s with a fade while on battery or charging, 'FULLY CHARGED' when full, 'THRESHOLD' when a charge limit holds; the column stops 10px left of the big percent; on the right the percent from the battery script, e.g. '87%', at displayLarge 28px bold foreground ('—' before the first read). (2) Battery bar, 8px tall pill (radius 4): track foreground alpha 0.12, fill foreground at width max(8, w x charge), pulsing opacity 1 to 0.55 while charging. (3) Stats, two 180px columns 20px apart, each two label/value lines 4px apart at bodySmall 11px, label foreground at opacity 0.6 on the left, value foreground pushed right: left column 'Battery size 53Wh' / 'Charge cycles 112'; right column 'Time left 3h 12m' / 'Discharging 13.1W' on battery, 'Time to full 45m' / 'Charging 24.6W' on AC, or 'Charge limit 75-80%' / 'Battery state Holding' when held at a threshold. Hidden until the first script read. (4) PanelSeparator 1px. (5) Power profile block, Column spacing 10: PanelSectionHeader 'POWER PROFILE', then a Row of equal bordered Buttons 6px apart (3 profiles: (380-12)/3 = 122.67px each), each with a profile glyph (14px) left of its label (bodySmall 11px), padding 10px horizontal x 8px vertical, in order Power-saver, Balanced, Performance; the active profile is drawn selected (fill alpha 0.18), the cursor/hover one with the hover-cursor fill and border. No brightness, lock, suspend or other action rows exist in this panel.

network.layout: Bar widget: a 27px icon slot showing the connection glyph (see bar.json); any mouse button toggles the panel, no scroll handler, no tooltip unless the link is restricted. Panel content is 380px wide (fittedContentWidth(Style.space(380)), clamped to the screen) and as tall as its content plus the container inset. Content is one Column, spacing 12, top to bottom (hidden items take no space or spacing): (1) HERO, ~34px tall: on the left a 24px (display) connection glyph in bar.text (bar.active/urgent when restricted); 14px to its right a two-line label block (2px gap): the connection name in title 14px bold bar.text, e.g. 'Homenet' or 'Ethernet (1gbit)', elided; under it a caption 10px bold, letter-spacing 1.2, uppercase status in Qt.darker(bar.text,1.4), e.g. 'HAULING BYTES' (a phrase that cross-fades to the next every 2.8s while connected), 'NOT CONNECTED', or 'LIMITED INTERNET ACCESS' in urgent. On the right, vertically centred, a RowLayout (spacing 8) of up to three hero actions: QR-code button U+F0432 (29x29, only when connected to a non-enterprise Wi-Fi), speed-test button U+F04C5 (29x29, only when an interface exists), and the Wi-Fi radio ToggleSwitch (42x22 track, 54x34 with cursor ring; only when NetworkManager and a Wi-Fi device exist). The label block's right edge stops 12px before the actions. (2) CAPTIVE PORTAL BUTTON (only behind a portal): full-width bordered, active Button 'Sign into network' with icon U+F03CC, foreground and accent both urgent, 10px vertical padding. (3) DETAILS GRID (only when an interface is up): 4 columns (label, value, label, value), column spacing 20, row spacing 4, four rows: Ping | '12 ms' | Packet Loss | '0%'; Receiving | '1.2 KB/s' | Sending | '312 B/s'; Downloaded | '1.84 GB' | Uploaded | '210.5 MB'; IP Address | '192.168.1.42' | Gateway | '192.168.1.1'. Labels bodySmall 11px bar.text at 0.6 opacity; values bodySmall 11px bar.text right-aligned, filling their column; ping/loss values turn urgent when loss > 0. IP and gateway click to copy. Each row ~15px; grid ~72px. (4) 1px PanelSeparator, then WI-FI BAND section (only on Wi-Fi with >1 band available or a band pinned): Column spacing 10; a header line with PanelSectionHeader 'WI-FI BAND: 5GHZ' (under Automatic) or 'WI-FI BAND' (pinned) on the left and, on the right, a Row (spacing 6) of PanelSectionHeader 'AUTOMATIC' plus a small ToggleSwitch (12px tall track, 23 wide, 29x18 with its 3px cursor pad) checked while Automatic. Under Automatic the pills are collapsed (height 0); when a band is pinned a row of equal-width bordered pills (spacing 6) slides open over 140ms: '2.4ghz' '5ghz' ('6ghz'), bodySmall 11px, padding 10 x 8; the band in use has the selected fill, the pinned band is bold. (5) 1px separator, then DNS PROVIDER section: Column spacing 10; PanelSectionHeader 'DNS PROVIDER'; a Row (spacing 6) of four equal pills, each (380-18)/4 = 90.5px wide: 'DHCP' 'Cloudflare' 'Google' 'Custom', bodySmall 11px, padding 10 x 8, bordered; the current provider has the selected fill (0.18). (6) 1px separator (only when a Wi-Fi device exists), then the NETWORK LIST: a clipped ListView, height min(contentHeight, 240), 4px between delegates, scrollbar as needed. Each delegate is a Column (4px gap) of an optional section header ('KNOWN NETWORKS' above the first row if it is known, 'OTHER NETWORKS' above the first unknown row) and a NetworkRow. Rows sort connected first, then known, then by signal descending. A row has 10px left/right inner margins and is ~30px tall for one line (tallest child + 12) or ~42px with a status line: Wi-Fi strength glyph (title 14px) at left; 10px gap; SSID in body 12px bar.text (elided; 'Hidden' when blank) with, under it (1px gap), a caption 10px status line ('Connected', 'Connecting…', 'Sign-in required', a failure reason) that is absent when empty; at the right a 22px-wide slot (8px gap before it) holding a lock U+F033E (subtitle 13px, Qt.darker(bar.text,1.4)) for secured networks or a Forget U+F0159 in urgent for known, unconnected networks. The connected row carries the selected fill (foreground alpha 0.18, no border); the cursor row the hover fill (0.08) with a 1px 0.25 border. Glyph and status colour: bar.text when connected or busy, urgent when failed or behind a portal, otherwise Qt.darker(bar.text,1.5). Choosing a secured unknown network expands that row in place into a passphrase prompt: a 30px password TextField (placeholder 'Passphrase') beside a 23x23 check button U+F012C, preceded by an 'Identity (user@domain)' field for WPA-EAP; while connecting or after a failure the fields become a 28px bordered message box reading 'Connecting…' or 'Wrong password' (urgent). Typical example (laptop on dual-band Wi-Fi 'Homenet', 78% signal, Automatic band, DHCP DNS, 5 networks in range): hero ~34, details ~72, band header ~18, DNS ~58, list of 'KNOWN NETWORKS' header + 2 rows and 'OTHER NETWORKS' header + 3 rows, ~230px, so the content is ~490px tall plus the container inset.

items.what: Passphrase TextField: placeholder 'Passphrase' (Qt.darker(fg,1.6)), password echo, body 12px, padding 8 x 6 plus 1px border, so ~30px tall; normal fill alpha 0.04 / border 0.4, focused or hovered fill 0.08 / border 0.25; 4px bottom margin; right edge 6px before the check button. Autofocuses. Enter submits; Esc cancels
items.expr: password: true; placeholderText: I18n.t("network.passphrase"); font.pixelSize: Style.font.body; horizontalPadding: Style.spacing.controlGap; verticalPadding: Style.spacing.controlPaddingY; anchors.bottomMargin: Style.spacing.rowGap / 2; anchors.rightMargin: Style.space(6); onAccepted: row.submitCredentials(); Keys.onEscapePressed: root.cancelPasswordPrompt()

items.what: Enterprise (WPA/WPA2-EAP) only: identity TextField above the passphrase, placeholder 'Identity (user@domain)', same styling; takes focus first; Enter moves to the passphrase. Credentials go to nmcli over stdin (PEAP/MSCHAPv2)
items.expr: visible: row.isEnterprise && !row.isBusy && !row.isFailed; placeholderText: I18n.t("network.identity"); onAccepted: pwField.forceActiveFocus()

items.what: Submit PanelActionButton: check glyph U+F012C, default icon font 14 so size round(max(22, 14+8)) | 1 = 23; tooltip 'Connect'; enabled only with a passphrase (and identity for enterprise)
items.expr: iconText: "󰄬"; tooltipText: I18n.t("network.connect"); enabled: row.net && pwField.text.length > 0 && (!row.isEnterprise || idField.text.length > 0)

items.what: While connecting or after failure the fields and button hide and a full-width 28px box shows (normal fill 0.04, normal border 0.4/1px, radius 0) with centred bodySmall 11px text: 'Connecting…' in bar.text or 'Wrong password' in urgent. After 2000ms a failure clears and the passphrase field refocuses
items.expr: height: Style.spacing.controlHeight; color: Style.normalFillFor(root.bar.foreground); borderSpec: Border.controlSpec("normal", ...); text: row.isFailed ? I18n.t("network.wrongPassword") : I18n.t("network.connecting"); failureTimer interval: 2000

items.what: A panel-started connect that fails with NoSecrets or WifiAuthTimeout on a secured network reopens the passphrase prompt
On open: cursor section = portal if behind a portal (cursor shown), else the Wi-Fi list at row 0 if any rows, else DNS; cursor hidden (cursorActive false) until the first key or hover
When the cursor is hidden, the first j/Down/h/l/Left/Right only reveals it; k/Up reveals and moves

j/Down and k/Up walk sections top to bottom: header actions -> portal -> band (Automatic switch, then pills when pinned) -> DNS -> Wi-Fi rows; hidden sections are skipped; k on the first Wi-Fi row returns to DNS (no wrap)
h/Left and l/Right: move among hero actions (QR, speed, switch), band pills, DNS pills; on a Wi-Fi row, l moves to its Forget slot (only if forgettable) and h back
items.expr: if (focusSection === "header") selectHeaderByDelta(dx) else if ("band") { if (!bandAutoFocused) selectBandByDelta(dx) } else if ("dns") selectDnsByDelta(dx) else if ("wifi") selectWifiActionByDelta(dx)

items.what: Enter/Return/Space (only when the cursor is visible): header -> QR / speed test / Wi-Fi toggle; portal -> open portal; band -> toggle Automatic or pin pill; DNS -> set provider; Wi-Fi row -> forget (if on the Forget slot), disconnect (connected), passphrase prompt (secured, unknown) or connect

Letter keys: r/R refresh (details, DNS, band, list; no forced rescan); w/W toggle the Wi-Fi radio. Esc closes; Tab/Shift+Tab switches to the next/previous bar panel. x/Delete emit deleteRequested, which this panel does not handle
items.expr: onTextKey: function(t) { if (t === "r" || t === "R") root.refresh() else if (t === "w" || t === "W") root.toggleNetwork() }; onCloseRequested: root.close(); onTabRequested: root.switchPanel(direction)

items.what: All panel keys are blocked while the passphrase prompt is open; the text field owns input (Enter submit, Esc cancel). Focus returns to the key catcher when the prompt closes
IPC methods on target omarchy.network: open, close, show, hide, toggle, toggleNetwork, showQr (summons wifiqr with self-detection), speedTest, openCaptivePortal, checkConnectivity
items.expr: ShellIpc { target: "omarchy.network"; function open() ... function showQr() { root.summonWifiQr(true) } ... }

items.what: Opening forces a rescan: scanner disabled, re-enabled after 100ms, list synced 1500ms later; scanner released on close

bluetooth.layout: Bar widget: one BarIconButton glyph (U+F00AF on, U+F00B1 a device connected, U+F00B2 off; the widget is hidden when there is no adapter). The panel card holds a 380px-wide content column (spacing 14). Typical case, adapter on, one connected headset with battery, two paired, scanning found two: (1) Hero row, about 34px tall (the tallest of the 24px glyph, the label stack and the 54x34 ToggleSwitch). Left: a Bluetooth glyph at display 24px in foreground (opacity 0.5 when off). 14px gap, then a label column (spacing 2): 'Bluetooth' at title 14px bold foreground, and under it a rotating phrase in caps, e.g. 'UNTANGLING WIRES', at caption 10px bold, letterSpacing 1.2, colour Qt.darker(foreground,1.4). The phrase fades out over 150ms, changes and fades in over 200ms, every 2800ms. Right edge: ToggleSwitch (track 42x22, 6px cursor pad, so 54x34). The labels stop 66px from the right edge (switch width + 12). (2) 14px gap, a 1px PanelSeparator. (3) 14px gap, the CONNECTED block (column spacing 10): the PanelSectionHeader 'CONNECTED' (caption 10 bold, darker 1.4), then a device row about 42px tall. (4) 14px gap, a separator, shown only when both the connected list and the scroll list have rows. (5) 14px gap, a ListView up to 400px tall (clipped; scrollbar as needed; 10px between delegates). Each delegate is a column (spacing 10): a separator before a section's first row unless it is the very first row, then the section header 'PAIRED' or 'AVAILABLE' on the section's first row, then the device row. AVAILABLE appears only while the adapter is discovering, and the panel keeps discovery on while it is open. Device row: a CursorSurface, full width. Height = content + 12, so 6px above and below. Inner margins are 10 left and 10 right. In the row: a Bluetooth glyph at heading 16px (U+F00B1 connected, U+F00AF otherwise; there are no per-device-type glyphs), a 10px gap, then a two-line info column (spacing 1). Line 1 is the device name at body 12, foreground, elided. Line 2 is the status at caption 10, shown only when it is non-empty: battery '80%', 'Connecting…', 'Disconnecting…', 'Forgetting…' or 'Connected'. On the right of a hovered or cursor-selected paired or connected row sits a 23x23 PanelActionButton with the close-circle glyph U+F0159, 8px from the info column. A connected row has the selected fill (foreground alpha 0.18, no border). The row under the cursor has the hover fill (foreground alpha 0.08) and a 1px border (alpha 0.25). With no connected devices and no rows in the list, a wrapped bodySmall 11px line in Qt.darker(foreground,1.5) replaces the lists: 'Scanning for devices…', 'Turn Bluetooth on to scan' or 'No Bluetooth adapter'. Heights assume JetBrainsMono line height ≈1.32em (12px≈16, 10px≈13, 16px≈21); the real values are font metrics at runtime.

items.what: Panel content width
Panel content height: the content's implicit height, with no cap beyond the available card height
Gap between top-level blocks (hero, separators, connected list, scroll list, empty text)
Bar and hero glyph by state
items.value: no adapter: "" (widget hidden); off: U+F00B2; any device connected: U+F00B1; on: U+F00AF
items.expr: if (!adapter) return ""; if (!adapter.enabled) return "󰂲"; if (connectedDevices.length > 0) return "󰂱"; return "󰂯"

items.what: Bar widget is shown only when an adapter exists
Bar widget mouse: right click turns the power on or off; left and middle click open or close the panel; the wheel does nothing
items.expr: onPressed: function(b) { if (b === Qt.RightButton) root.toggleBluetooth() else root.toggle() }

items.what: Bar widget tooltip: none. No tooltipText is set, and the bar shows nothing for empty text
items.expr: BarIconButton { text: root.icon } (no tooltipText); showTooltip: if (!text) return

items.what: Power toggle runs the rfkill helper with an explicit direction (Powered follows it)
Hero row height: the max of glyph, labels and switch
Hero glyph: same glyph as the bar, display size, foreground, dimmed when off
items.expr: font.pixelSize: Style.font.display; color: root.bar.foreground; opacity: root.adapter && root.adapter.enabled ? 1.0 : 0.5

items.what: Label column: 14px after the glyph; right margin = switch width + 12
items.expr: anchors.leftMargin: Style.space(14); anchors.rightMargin: powerSwitch.visible ? powerSwitch.width + Style.space(12) : 0; spacing: Style.space(2)

items.what: Title text
items.expr: Commons.I18n.t("bluetooth.title"); font.pixelSize: Style.font.title (14); font.bold: true; color: root.bar.foreground; elide right

items.what: Status line, upper-cased. No adapter: 'NO ADAPTER'. Off: 'TURNED OFF'. On: rotating phrases
items.expr: root.heroStatusText.toUpperCase(); font.pixelSize: Style.font.caption (10); bold; letterSpacing 1.2; color: Qt.darker(root.bar.foreground, 1.4)

items.what: Rotating phrases while the adapter is on, in order
Phrase cycle: every 2800ms while open and on. Fade out to 0 over 150ms (OutCubic), advance, fade in to 1 over 200ms (OutCubic)
items.expr: Timer { interval: 2800; running: root.opened && root.rotatingPhrases }; PropertyAnimation opacity to 0.0 duration Style.duration(150); to 1.0 duration Style.duration(200)

items.what: Power ToggleSwitch on the hero's right edge. Props: visible: !!adapter; checked: adapter.enabled; hasCursor: cursor on the virtual 'header' section; foreground: bar.foreground. Hovering puts the cursor on the header. Toggling calls toggleBluetooth()
items.expr: ToggleSwitch { visible: !!root.adapter; checked: !!root.adapter && root.adapter.enabled; hasCursor: root.headerHasCursor; onHovered: setHeaderCursor(); onToggled: root.toggleBluetooth() }

items.what: Switch tooltip (PanelToolTip, shown on mouse hover)
items.value: 'Turn Bluetooth off' when on / 'Turn Bluetooth on' when off

items.what: PanelSeparator under the hero, always shown (1px, foreground at strength 0.12)
Connected block: column with spacing 10. PanelSectionHeader 'CONNECTED', then one DeviceRow per connected device. Shown only when a device is connected
items.expr: visible: root.connectedDevices.length > 0; spacing: Style.space(10); PanelSectionHeader { text: I18n.t("bluetooth.connected") }

items.what: Separator between the connected block and the scroll list, only when both have rows
Scroll list (ListView): paired rows, then discovered rows. Height capped at 400; clipped; scrollbar AsNeeded; flickable only when overflowing
items.expr: height: Math.min(contentHeight, Style.space(400)); spacing: Style.space(10); clip: true; ScrollBar.vertical policy AsNeeded

items.what: Each list delegate is a column (spacing 10): a separator if the row starts a section and is not first, the section header on a section's first row, then the DeviceRow
items.expr: PanelSeparator { visible: index > 0 && sectionTitle !== "" }; PanelSectionHeader { visible: sectionTitle !== "" }

items.what: Section header strings in the scroll list

How devices are grouped. Devices with no human name (empty, UUID-like or MAC-like) are dropped. Connected → 'connected'. Paired, bonded or trusted → 'known'. Anything else → 'discovered'. Each group is sorted by label with localeCompare. Discovered rows show only while adapter.discovering
While the panel is open and the adapter is on, discovery is re-requested every 1000ms whenever it is not running. After close, StopDiscovery is retried every 1000ms, at most 3 times
items.expr: Timer { interval: 1000; repeat: true; triggeredOnStart: true; running: root.opened && root.adapter.enabled && !root.adapter.discovering }

items.what: Device row height: content + rowPaddingX (12), with content centred, so 6 above and below. Content = max(16px glyph ≈21, info column, 23px forget button; the button's implicit height counts even when hidden). ≈35 with no status line, ≈42 with one
items.expr: implicitHeight: rowContent.implicitHeight + Style.spacing.rowPaddingX; rowContent.implicitHeight: Math.max(deviceIcon.implicitHeight, info.implicitHeight, forgetBtn.implicitHeight)

items.what: Row inner left and right margins
Row glyph at heading size, coloured statusColor. U+F00B1 when connected, else U+F00AF. No device-type glyphs
items.expr: text: row.isConnected ? "󰂱" : "󰂯"; font.pixelSize: Style.font.heading; color: row.statusColor

items.what: Info column: 10px after the glyph, spacing 1. It stops 8px before the forget button when that is visible
items.expr: anchors.leftMargin: Style.space(10); spacing: Style.space(1); anchors.rightMargin: forgetBtn.visible ? Style.space(8) : 0

items.what: Device name: body 12, foreground, elided right. Falls back to 'Device'
items.expr: root.deviceLabel(row.dev) || I18n.t("bluetooth.device"); font.pixelSize: Style.font.body; color: root.bar.foreground

items.what: Status line (caption 10, statusColor; hidden when empty). Checked in order: pending forget → 'Forgetting…'; pending disconnect or state 2 → 'Disconnecting…'; connected → battery 'N%' if available, else '' in the connected section ('Connected' elsewhere); pending connect, state 3 or pairing → 'Connecting…'; otherwise ''
items.expr: if (action === "forgetting") ...; if (isConnected) { if (dev.batteryAvailable) return I18n.formatNumber(Math.round(dev.battery * 100)) + "%"; return sectionName === "connected" ? "" : I18n.t("bluetooth.connectedStatus") } ...

items.what: Glyph and status colour: foreground when connected or busy (pending action, state 3, pairing); else Qt.darker(foreground,1.5)
items.expr: if (isConnected) return root.bar.foreground; if (action !== "" || devState === 3 || dev.pairing === true) return root.bar.foreground; return Qt.darker(root.bar.foreground, 1.5)

items.what: Row surface (CursorSurface). Under the cursor (hasCursor = row selected and the forget button not focused): hover fill, foreground alpha 0.08, with the hover-cursor border (1px, alpha 0.25). Connected row (current): selected fill, foreground alpha 0.18, border width 0. Otherwise transparent. Colour animates over 60ms. Radius = cornerRadius (0)
items.expr: hasCursor: rowSelected && !root.actionFocused; current: isConnected; fill: root.hoverFill (Style.hoverFillFor(bar.foreground, accent)); currentFill: root.selectedFill (Style.selectedFillFor(...))

items.what: Forget button: PanelActionButton, close-circle glyph, at the right edge, vertically centred. Shown on paired or connected rows that are hovered or cursor-selected. hasCursor when the row is selected and actionFocused. Hover focuses it. Click forgets. Tooltip 'Forget'
items.expr: iconText: "󰅙"; tooltipText: I18n.t("bluetooth.forget"); visible: row.showForgetButton; hasCursor: row.rowSelected && root.actionFocused

items.what: Row tooltip on mouse hover (hidden while the forget button is focused): 'Disconnect' for connected, 'Pair' for discovered, 'Connect' for paired
items.expr: if (isConnected) return I18n.t("bluetooth.disconnect"); if (isDiscovered) return I18n.t("bluetooth.pair"); return I18n.t("bluetooth.connect")

items.what: Row mouse. Hover moves the cursor to the row. Left click: connected → disconnect; otherwise connect (pair if not yet paired). Right click: connected → disconnect; paired → forget; discovered → nothing. Pointing-hand cursor
items.expr: onClicked: if (mouse.button === Qt.RightButton) { if (row.isConnected) disconnectDevice(dev) else if (!row.isDiscovered) forgetDevice(dev); return } if (row.isConnected) disconnectDevice(dev) else connectDevice(dev)

items.what: Device actions run 'omarchy-bluetooth-device <action> <address>' detached. Connect: 'connect' if paired, bonded or trusted, else 'pair'. Disconnect also calls device.disconnect(). Forget: 'forget'. Each action sets the pending state 'connecting', 'disconnecting' or 'forgetting'
All pending action markers clear 20s after the last action, or as soon as BlueZ shows the result
items.expr: Timer { id: pendingTimeout; interval: 20000; onTriggered: root.pendingActions = ({}) }

items.what: When a connect finishes, the matching PipeWire sink becomes the default audio output. The sink is looked up every 500ms, up to 8 attempts
Empty-state line, shown when there are no connected devices and no list rows. bodySmall 11px, Qt.darker(foreground,1.5), word-wrapped to full width
items.value: 'No Bluetooth adapter' | 'Turn Bluetooth on to scan' | 'Scanning for devices…'

items.what: Opening the panel parks the cursor out of sight. It lands on the first connected device, else the first paired, else the first discovered, else the header (power switch). The first move key only shows the cursor
j/k and Down/Up step row by row: header (power switch) → connected → paired → discovered. Up from the first row goes to the header. No wrap
l/Right on a connected or paired row focuses its forget button (actionFocused). h/Left returns to the row. Discovered rows and the header ignore h/l
items.expr: moveCursorH(delta): if (delta > 0) actionFocused = true else if (delta < 0) actionFocused = false

items.what: Enter/Space (cursor shown). Header: power on or off. Forget button focused: forget. Connected row: disconnect. Paired row: connect. Discovered row: pair, then connect
x/X/Delete (cursor shown) forgets the selected connected or paired device
b/B turns the power on or off from anywhere in the panel, with or without a visible cursor
Esc closes the panel. Tab/Shift+Tab switches to the next or previous panel
IPC target omarchy.bluetooth
items.value: open, close, show, hide, toggle, toggleBluetooth

monitor.layout: Bar widget: a BarIconButton glyph, U+F037A (monitor-multiple) when Quickshell.screens.length > 1, else U+F0379 (monitor). It has no tooltip. The panel content is 380px wide, inside a ScrollView with the height capped at 860; one column with spacing 14. Each section is separated by a 1px PanelSeparator with a 14px gap above and below. Typical case: a laptop eDP-1 at 2880x1800@120, scale 2, brightness 60%, plus an external DP-1 (model 'DELL U2723QE') at 3840x2160@60, scale 1.5, to its right; the laptop is shown. (1) Hero, about 34px tall. Left: a glyph at display 24px in foreground, U+F0322 (laptop) for a built-in display, else U+F0379. 14px gap, then a label column (spacing 2, right margin 8): the display title at title 14px bold foreground ('Built-in Display'), and under it the brightness mood in caps, e.g. 'EVEN DAY', at caption 10px bold, letterSpacing 1.2, Qt.darker(foreground,1.4). With more than one display, the right edge (6px in) holds a picker: one 14px glyph per display, 14px apart. The shown display's glyph is accent; the others are Qt.darker(foreground,1.55) until hovered or picked, then foreground. Each picker glyph has a tooltip 'Built-in Display · eDP-1'. (2) BRIGHTNESS, only if the shown display's brightness can be read. A header row: 'BRIGHTNESS' on the left, '60%' on the right 6px in (caption 10 bold, darker 1.4). 6px gap, then a 30px slider row (CursorSurface outline; PanelSlider 1..100 with 6px side insets). (3) TEXT SIZE, always present. Header 'TEXT SIZE' with '12px' on the right. 6px gap, then a 30px slider row: a 7-notch PanelSlider over the stops 9/10/11/12/14/16/20 px. (4) SCALE: header 'SCALE'. Then a gap of 19px (6 + sliderInset 13), then one grid row of bordered pill Buttons, 3px apart, splitting the width equally: '1x 1.25x 1.6x 2x 3x 4x' (about 61px each), each about 27px tall. 13px bottom padding. The current scale is active. (5) RESOLUTION, only when the display offers more than one same-aspect size of at least 1080p. Header 'RESOLUTION' with the exact mode on the right ('3840×2160'), then pills such as '1080p 1440p 4K', laid out like SCALE. (6) REFRESH RATE, only when the current resolution offers at least two whole rates of 60Hz or more and one is above 60. Header with '120 Hz' on the right, then pills '60 120'. (7) LAYOUT, shown when there is more than one box to arrange or when Mirror is available. Header 'LAYOUT' on the left. On the right, 6px in, two plain-text links 14px apart, 'Mirror' and 'Extend' (caption 10); the current mode is accent bold. 6px gap. Then a map row, map height + 26, holding the arrangement map with 6px side insets. Each display is a box at its logical size times the ratio, minus 2px, centred. The shown display has the selected fill and an accent border; the others have the hover fill and a Qt.darker(foreground,1.6) border; all boxes are backed by popups.background. Each box's connector name is centred in caption 10, bold on the shown display. For the typical pair: ratio = min(368*0.8/4000, 100/1440) ≈ 0.0694, so the map is 100px tall, eDP-1 is ≈98x60 and DP-1 ≈176x98, side by side and top-aligned. 6px gap, then a centred hint in caption 10, Qt.darker(foreground,1.55). Its space is always reserved, and it is opaque only while the map is hovered or has the cursor: 'ctrl+arrows or drag to arrange · r to rotate'. Right-clicking a box, or pressing r, opens a 148px-wide rotate menu (popups.background, popups.border 1px, 4px padding) with the rows Normal / 90° / 180° / 270°. A layout with no movable displays shows only the hero, (brightness), text size and scale. Heights assume JetBrainsMono line height ≈1.32em; the real values are font metrics at runtime.

items.what: Panel content width
Content height: the implicit height capped at 860 (and at the available card height). Taller content scrolls in the ScrollView, whose vertical bar appears only when overflowing
Gap between top-level blocks (hero, separators, sections)
Shared inset: (slider row height - track height) / 2 = (30 - 4) / 2. Pads pill rows and the map so every section shows the same gap
Bar glyph
items.value: U+F037A when more than one screen, else U+F0379

items.what: Bar widget: any click (left, right or middle) opens or closes the panel. Wheel: the focused display's brightness ±5% per notch (Util.wheelSteps accumulates touchpad deltas, clamping each event to ±120), then the brightness OSD is summoned. The wheel does nothing when brightness is unavailable
Bar widget tooltip: none (no tooltipText is set)

State comes from 'omarchy-monitor-state', run at load, at each open, every 5000ms while open, and after each command. Output lines: 0 focused brightness; 1 internal; 2 external; 3 internal enabled; 4 mirror; 5 focused; 6 scale; 7 displays JSON (name, make, model, enabled, focused, width, height, refreshRate, scale, x, y, transform, mirrorOf, availableModes, brightness); 8 'on' if Omarchy's mirror toggle is on
items.expr: Process { command: ["omarchy-monitor-state"] }; Timer { interval: 5000; running: root.opened }

items.what: Displays listed in the picker: those enabled with width > 0, in Hyprland's order. Title: built-in (eDP/LVDS/DSI) → 'Built-in Display'; else the model, unless it is a hex code; else the make; else the connector
Hero row height: the max of glyph, labels and picker
Hero glyph: display 24px, foreground. U+F0322 (laptop) for a built-in display, else U+F0379 (monitor)
items.expr: text: root.displayGlyph(root.current); displayGlyph: entry && entry.builtIn ? "󰌢" : "󰍹"; font.pixelSize: Style.font.display

items.what: Label column: 14px after the glyph, right margin 8 (to the picker, or to the edge), spacing 2
items.expr: anchors.leftMargin: Style.space(14); anchors.rightMargin: Style.space(8); spacing: Style.space(2)

items.what: Title: the shown display's title, else 'Display'. title 14px bold foreground, elided
Subtitle: the brightness mood name in caps, or 'FIXED BRIGHTNESS' when the brightness cannot be controlled. caption 10 bold, letterSpacing 1.2, Qt.darker(foreground,1.4)
Mood names by rounded percent
items.value: >=95 Sun blast; >=80 Solar flare; >=65 Golden hour; >=45 Even day; >=30 Soft glow; >=20 Lamp light; >=10 Candlelit; else Night owl

items.what: Display picker, shown with more than one display: a Row, spacing 14, right margin 6, one glyph per display at icon 14px. Colour: accent if shown; foreground if hovered or under the keyboard cursor; else Qt.darker(foreground,1.55). No box. Hit area grows 6px on each side. Click shows that display; hover puts the cursor on it
items.expr: color: current ? Commons.Color.accent : (hot ? root.bar.foreground : Qt.darker(root.bar.foreground, 1.55)); font.pixelSize: Style.font.icon

items.what: Picker glyph tooltip: title · connector
The BRIGHTNESS section (and its separator) shows only when the shown display reports a numeric brightness
Header row: 'BRIGHTNESS' on the left. On the right, 6px in, the value 'N%' (the live drag value while dragging), caption 10 bold, Qt.darker(foreground,1.4). Column spacing to the slider row is 6

Slider row: a CursorSurface (outline) of height slider + controlGap = 22 + 8. The PanelSlider has 6px side insets; minimum 1, maximum 100, step 1, integer; value max(1, brightness). Moving previews it, with the set debounced by 180ms; release sets it at once. Hovering puts the cursor on the row
items.expr: height: brightnessSlider.implicitHeight + Style.spacing.controlGap; PanelSlider { minimum: 1; maximum: 100; step: 1; integer: true; value: Math.max(1, root.currentBrightness) }

items.what: Set command, per display. One runs at a time; the latest value is queued. The panel does not re-read after a set

Where brightness comes from: an Apple display → omarchy-brightness-display-apple; an external display with DDC → omarchy-brightness-display-ddc; the built-in panel → brightnessctl backlight. An external display without DDC reports nothing, so the section hides
items.expr: if use_apple_display ... elif use_ddc_display ... elif ! use_backlight_display; then exit 1

items.what: Header 'TEXT SIZE' with the px value on the right, 6px in: the pending stop, else Style.font.baseSize. caption 10 bold, darker 1.4

Text size slider row: always shown, 30px, 6px insets. Index slider 0..6 with tickCount 7 over the stops [9,10,11,12,14,16,20] px. Release runs 'omarchy-display-text-size <px>'. The size is shared by all displays and reflows the whole shell, this panel included
items.expr: textSizeStops: [9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 20]; PanelSlider { minimum: 0; maximum: root.textSizeStops.length - 1; tickCount: root.textSizeStops.length; value: root.currentTextIndex() }

items.what: Scale presets, filtered per mode: each preset snaps to a scale that divides the mode cleanly (in 1/120 units of gcd(w,h)), and presets that snap to the same value are merged. 2880x1800, 1920x1080 and 3840x2160 keep all six. For 2560x1440, 3 shows as 3.2

SCALE section: a header, then a single-row grid. Column spacing = 6 + sliderInset = 19; bottom padding = sliderInset = 13. Grid columns = number of scales, spacing xs = 3, cell width = (W - 3(n-1))/n ≈ (380-15)/6 ≈ 60.8 at full width
items.expr: spacing: Style.space(6) + panelColumn.sliderInset; bottomPadding: panelColumn.sliderInset; Grid { columns: current.scales.length; spacing: Style.spacing.xs; cellWidth: (width - spacing * (columns - 1)) / columns }

items.what: Scale, resolution and refresh pills are shared Buttons with fontSize caption 10, horizontalPadding sm 4, verticalPadding controlPaddingY 6 and bordered. active = the current value; hasCursor = keyboard or hover cursor. Height ≈ 13 line + 12 + 2 border ≈ 27
items.expr: fontSize: Style.font.caption; horizontalPadding: Style.spacing.sm; verticalPadding: Style.spacing.controlPaddingY; bordered: true

agents.layout: One card (content 380px wide, height = content + 32px inset, capped at 860px and at the screen; scrolls past that) listing every subscription on one page, limits first. Inks are the bar's colours: 'foreground' is bar.text and 'urgent' is bar.active (both default to the theme foreground/urgent); 'dim' is Qt.darker(foreground, 1.55). A Column with 16px spacing, top to bottom, for a typical machine with Claude Code (Max 20x) and Codex (Pro 200): (1) HERO, about 34px tall (the tallest part is the 34x34 add button). On the left is the agents glyph U+F16A3 at 24px in foreground. 14px to its right are two lines 2px apart: 'Agents' (title 14px bold, foreground) and a rotating summary in caption 10px bold, uppercased, letter-spacing 1.2, in Qt.darker(foreground, 1.4), e.g. '41.2M TOKENS THIS WEEK'. It cross-fades every 2.8s through: tokens today, 'MOSTLY OPUS 4.8', 'BUSIEST DAY: TUESDAY', '37 PROMPTS TODAY', '6 SESSIONS TODAY'. Right-aligned is a 34x34 square in accent at 0.12 alpha holding U+F0415 (plus) at 16px in accent. (2) CLAUDE SECTION, a Column with 16px spacing. First a 1px separator in foreground at 0.12. Then the header row, about 16px tall: the Claude logo at 16x16; 10px gap; 'Claude Code' in body 12px bold foreground; 8px gap; 'Max 20x' in caption 10px dim, on the same baseline; a 23x23 terminal button U+F07B7 at the right edge, centred vertically and taller than the row. Then the limit lines with 12px between them. Each line is a 114px title column ('Session', then 'Weekly'; bodySmall 11px foreground), then a 4px-thick meter with fully rounded ends (radius 2) from x=114 to 20px before the value column, then a right-aligned value column as wide as '00h 00m' at 11px (about 47px) in dim showing time to reset: '2h 13m' and '3d 4h'. The meter track is foreground at 0.18 and the fill is foreground, 42% and 61% wide. The Weekly meter also carries a 2x10px tick at 30% for the model-scoped 'Fable Weekly' allowance. (3) CODEX SECTION, the same shape: separator; header 'Codex' with 'Pro 200' and a terminal button; 'Session' at 12% ('4h 2m'); 'Weekly' at 93% ('1d 6h'). Its fill and ticks turn urgent because the percent is 0.9 or more. That also makes the bar icon urgent. (4) A 1px separator. (5) 'MAKE SOMETHING COOL' (PanelSectionHeader), 12px gap, then a row of three 120px-wide tiles 10px apart. Each tile is foreground at 0.05 with square corners, about 36px tall (content + 20), and holds a 16px accent glyph and a 12px bold label 8px apart: U+F03D8 Theme, U+F0431 Plugin, U+F08C6 App. (6) A centred caption footer in dim, shown only with sync on ('Merged from 2 devices'). Other shapes: a prepaid provider shows a Balance line (title, a draining meter, the amount right-aligned in a 96px column) and a 'spent of funded' caption in place of limit lines. A provider with 2+ accounts shows one block per account: a name line with the plan after it and 'ACTIVE' or 'Use' on the right, then that account's limit lines. A lapsed Claude/Codex/Grok sign-in adds an urgent 'Sign-in required' link under the header. Any other trouble adds a dim U+F02FD info mark after the plan; its tooltip explains. With nothing set up, the hero line reads 'ADD AN ACCOUNT', there is no + button, and the body is a separator, an intro caption, and Claude Code / Codex / Grok as large marks three across with the first lit.

Account name: label or id; body 12px, bold if active, accent when picked by the keyboard, else foreground; underlined on hover with an IBeam cursor; at most 60% of the width, elided. Tooltip shows the email. A click renames in place
items.expr: width: Math.min(implicitWidth, parent.width * 0.6); color: head.picked ? Commons.Color.accent : root.foreground; font.bold: head.isActive; font.underline: nameMouse.containsMouse

items.what: After the name (8px gap, Row spacing 8): '· <plan>[ · N free resets]' in caption 10px dim, then the info mark, then '·' plus an urgent 'Sign-in required' link when needed (tooltip 'Sign in to this account again')
Right side of the active account's line
items.expr: text: Commons.I18n.t("agents.active"); color: Commons.Color.accent; font.bold: true

items.what: Right side of an inactive account: Row (spacing 12) of TextLinks. 'Autoswitch' shows when auto mode is on, the line is hovered, or it is picked; it is current (accent, bold) when on. 'Use' shows when auto is off, hovered, or picked. A picked link gets the suffix ' U+23CE'. Autoswitch tooltip: 'Switch here automatically at 95%' or 'Stop switching automatically'
Inline rename field (TextField, body 12px, padding 4/1). Enter saves through omarchy-agent-account-rename; Esc or losing focus cancels. Panel keys are blocked while renaming
items.expr: horizontalPadding: Style.space(4); verticalPadding: Style.space(1); onAccepted: head.finishRename(true)

items.what: A PanelSeparator, then a Column (spacing 12) with a PanelSectionHeader. Hidden while adding or on a blank slate
Three tiles, 10px apart, each (width - 20)/3

Tile: content height + 20, radius cornerRadius (0). Fill foreground at 0.05, accent at 0.14 under the cursor. Centred Row (spacing 8) of the glyph (heading 16px, accent) and the label (body 12px bold, foreground, accent under the cursor)
items.expr: implicitHeight: tileBody.implicitHeight + Style.space(20); color: hasCursor ? root.alpha(Commons.Color.accent, 0.14) : root.alpha(root.foreground, 0.05)

items.what: Starter tiles. A click closes the panel and runs omarchy-agent-prompt <prompt>
items.expr: { glyph: "\u{F03D8}", label: Commons.I18n.t("agents.theme"), prompt: "Make me a new Omarchy theme. ..." }

items.what: Tile tooltip
items.value: Start your default agent on a new theme

items.what: Footer: centred caption 10px in dim, topPadding 2. Shows the sync error text, or 'Merged from N device(s)' when sync merged data. Hidden otherwise
items.expr: text: root.footerText(); color: root.dim; font.pixelSize: Style.font.caption; horizontalAlignment: Text.AlignHCenter

items.what: Blank slate: no enabled provider with data, no add-check result other than 'first', and no local model. The panel is then the picker
items.expr: readonly property bool blankSlate: usage.enabledProviders.length === 0 && !anySignedIn && !providers.some(function(p) { return !!p.localModel })

items.what: Hero line while picking or adding: 'Add an account' on a blank slate, 'Add another' from +, 'Add <Provider> account' once one is chosen (uppercased by PanelHero)
AddView (Column spacing 14, starting with a separator). On a blank slate it shows an intro caption, 10px dim, word-wrapped
items.value: Sign in to an AI coding subscription, and this panel keeps track of how much of it you have left.

items.what: Picker: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, plus 'Local AI' when a local recipe fits this machine. Row spacing 10; each choice is (width - 10*(n-1))/n wide (120 for 3, 87.5 for 4) and content + 16 tall. Column (spacing 10) of the logo at 24*1.6 = 38.4px (scale 1.08 under the cursor, 120ms OutQuad) and the name (body 12px bold, accent under the cursor). The first choice is lit on entry
items.expr: size: Style.font.display * 1.6; scale: choice.hasCursor ? 1.08 : 1.0; implicitHeight: choiceBody.implicitHeight + Style.space(16)

items.what: Local AI with nothing left to install: opacity 0.4 and a hover tooltip. Other unavailable choices (check state '') are not dimmed; clicking them does nothing and the cursor stays an arrow
items.expr: opacity: local && !available ? 0.4 : 1; cursorShape: choice.available ? Qt.PointingHandCursor : Qt.ArrowCursor

items.what: A second account asks for a name: caption hint in dim, then a TextField (body 12px, placeholder 'Work'). Enter starts the sign-in; Esc cancels
items.value: Name this account. It signs in through a private window, so your browser's current account isn't picked up.

items.what: Sign-in in progress (Column spacing 12): the status line (bodySmall 11px foreground; starts at 'Starting…', then '@@omarchy status' lines). If Grok's device code appears: the caption 'Confirm this code in your browser' and the code (XXXX-XXXX) in display 24px bold accent, letter-spacing 2. For Claude: a paste hint and a 'Code' field, which shows 'Checking the code…' after submit. A link 'Open the sign-in page again'
items.expr: text: root.addCode; color: Commons.Color.accent; font.pixelSize: Style.font.display; font.bold: true; font.letterSpacing: 2

items.what: Done or error text, bodySmall 11px: urgent on error, else foreground. If the process exits mid-run: 'The sign-in didn't finish.' 'done' returns to the list after 2500ms
items.expr: color: root.addStage === "error" ? root.urgent : root.foreground; Timer { id: addDoneTimer; interval: 2500 }

items.what: Local model section (from agent-local status.json). Header: vendor logo, the model name (elided), a play/pause PanelActionButton U+F040A/U+F03E4 (tooltip Start/Stop/'Not enough memory'; greyed to opacity 0.5 in dim when blocked) and a launch button U+F07B7 'Launch agent' while running. Below: a meter line titled 'Memory' (value '%1 GiB') or 'Loading'/'Stopping'/'Removing' with progress, or the error in urgent bodySmall
Bar widget glyph (BarIconButton). Always shown
Bar widget clicks: left toggles the panel; right runs 'omarchy-agent --pick' and closes; middle forces a refresh
items.expr: if (buttonCode === Qt.RightButton) root.launchAgent(); else if (buttonCode === Qt.MiddleButton) root.refreshNow(); else root.toggle()

items.what: Bar widget tooltip: none in any state. No tooltipText is set, and the bar shows no tooltip for empty text
items.expr: BarIconButton { id: button; bar: root.bar; text: ...; active: root.alarming; onPressed: ... }

items.what: IPC target omarchy.agents: open, close, show, hide, toggle, refresh (forced; returns 'ok')

Arrows or h/j/k/l move one cursor over the interactive stops in rows: hero +; per provider its line stop (terminal button, else the mark); the provider's Sign-in required link; per non-active account [signin], Autoswitch, Use; then the three starter tiles. While adding: the choices, or the local recipes. The first press only shows the cursor. Arriving on an account row lands on Use; on a provider line, its rightmost button. Hover moves the same cursor. While naming or signing in, Up/Down scroll by 56px
items.expr: onMoveRequested: ... root.moveKey(dx, dy) else if (dy !== 0) panelFlick.contentY = root.clamp(panelFlick.contentY + dy * Style.space(56), ...)

items.what: Enter or Space acts on the lit item: + or X, choice, recipe, play/pause, launch, starter, sign-in, autoswitch, or Use (switch the account). With nothing lit it forces a refresh
Text keys: r/R forces a refresh; m/M toggles autoswitch for the picked account's provider (else the first multi-account one); 1-9 picks that account across all providers (only when not adding)
items.expr: if (t === "r" || t === "R") root.refreshNow(); else if (t === "m" || t === "M") root.toggleSwitchMode(); else if (root.addStage === "" && t >= "1" && t <= "9" ...) root.pointAt("account", Number(t) - 1)

items.what: Ctrl+Up/Down or Ctrl+k/j moves the provider holding the cursor up or down (not while adding or renaming). Saved to order.json
Delete or x/X on a provider line opens a ConfirmDialog with the confirm button preselected. Confirming sets providers.<id>.enabled=false in the widget settings, or removes a local model's weights
items.value: Hide Codex from the panel? Credentials and sign-in will be kept.

items.what: Esc cancels a drag, else cancels adding, else closes. Tab/Shift+Tab switch to the neighbouring bar panel. Keys are blocked while renaming or while the confirm dialog is open
items.expr: onCloseRequested: { if (root.dragIndex >= 0) root.settleProviderDrag(true) else if (root.addStage !== "") root.cancelAdd() else root.close() }

items.what: Records regenerate on a repeating timer that also fires at start (omarchy-agent-usage-update). Default 900s, minimum 30s, setting refreshIntervalSec (UI range 30-3600 in steps of 30)
When a multi-account provider has any top-level window at >= min(0.8, (threshold-15)/100) (threshold default 95), the timer runs every min(180s, interval) in --limits-only mode
Opening the panel runs a --limits-only update, resets scroll to the top and the cursor, and re-runs the add check when nothing is enabled

Forced refresh (--force) from r, a middle click, Enter with nothing lit, or IPC refresh. Disabled providers are passed as --except <id>. A request made while a run is going queues one rerun; force outranks the others
Records with retryAdvised get one --limits-only rerun of just those ids 30s later
items.expr: Timer { id: limitsRetry; interval: 30000; repeat: false; onTriggered: root.runUpdate("limits", root.retryAgentIds) }

items.what: Records are ~/.local/state/omarchy/agents/usage/*.json, each watched by a FileView. After each update run the directory is rescanned and every record reloaded. An unparsable record is dropped
Providers with collectors (all enabled by default)

Record fields the panel reads: id, name, ready, tierLabel, usageStatusText, authHelpText, limits[{label,percent,resetsAt,title?}], limitsStale, limitsFetchedAt, retryAdvised, balance{remaining,funded,spent,currency,estimated}, accounts[{id,label,email,plan,active,primary,limits,stale,fetchedAt,usageStatusText,authHelpText,resetCredits?}], accountSwitch{mode,threshold}, resetCredits{available,nextExpiresAt}, plus the stats todayPrompts/todaySessions/todayTotalTokens/recentDays/modelUsage/hasPromptStats

elsewhen.layout: Bar: a 21px status-slot glyph button U+F01E7 (md-earth) in centerEnd right after the clock, tooltip "World clock". Left click toggles the panel; right or middle click re-runs the zone probe. Panel content is 340px wide (fittedContentWidth(340)) and as tall as its content, capped at 680 with the card's inset. The content is a scrollable Column, spacing panelGap 14, top to bottom: (1) HeroTitle, about 52px. An arched caption line (caption 10px, dim; accent while the time is scrubbed) reads "It's 12:00 PM here in New York". The glyphs sit on a shallow arc whose ends drop 6px. 2px below it is a centred row, spacing 9: "World" (title 14px DemiBold, foreground), a 31x31 drawn mini globe tilted 23.44deg, then "Clock" (title 14px DemiBold). (2) Only while the header search is open: a "Where are you?" CitySearch, with no button. (3) The stage, which holds the list or the globe. In list mode it holds one CityRow per tracked city, Column spacing md 6, each row about 70px tall and 340px wide (typical, with font metrics). Then panelGap 14, then a full-width bordered Button "+  Add a city" (~30px, bodySmall 11). A CityRow is an opaque rectangle whose fill is popups.background mixed toward foreground by time of day: 0.10 day, 0.07 dawn/dusk, 0.035 night. Hover adds 0.05; the picked row gets 0.15. Left column, inset 12: the city name (subtitle 13px DemiBold, foreground, elided), then flexible space, then the temperature (caption 10, dim) and a weather glyph (bodySmall 11, dim) set against the time column. Next comes an optional people line (overlapping avatars of 15px plus names, caption dim). Last is the date line: "Mon Nov 2", or for another day "Tue Nov 3 · Tomorrow" (caption 10). On hover the date crossfades to a local greeting such as "おやすみ oyasumi". Right column, inset 12, vertically centred on the labels: the time (heading 16px DemiBold, foreground; "--:--" before the probe lands), then the AM/PM caption on its baseline 3px right, then a line of zone abbreviation plus offset ("JST  +14h", caption, fainter). At the bottom, inset 12 each side and 15px above the row's bottom edge, sits the daylight strip. It is a 3px rounded track (foreground at 0.10) with lit spans (foreground at 0.28) from that day's real sunrise to sunset. On it is a 10px now-marker: a gold #E5C736 disc by day, or the moon's phase drawn in foreground by night. Hovering a row shows ↑/↓ sunrise and sunset arrows beside the lit band, plus two 20px circular buttons straddling the row's top-right corner: × (remove) and U+F0014 (account-plus, who's here). In globe mode (Space or a click on the mini globe) the rows are knocked off left and right, falling, tilting and shrinking. The stage grows to 378px and an orthographic globe scales up out of the mini globe's centre. The globe is a disc of about 149px radius on a 340x310 canvas: ocean, a 30deg graticule, bright land, a gold terminator, city dots and up to 14 labels. Below it are a 34px footer (selected city, its time, a home/tracked badge, its zone and offset) and a ~30px "Jump to a city" button. The header's mini globe turns into a × that leads back to the list.

items.what: Bar widget glyph (BarIconButton.text)
Bar button slot size
Bar tooltip, the same in every state
Bar mouse: left toggles the panel; right or middle refreshes the zone probe; no wheel handler in the panel
items.expr: if (buttonCode === Qt.RightButton || buttonCode === Qt.MiddleButton) root.refresh() else root.toggle()

items.what: Default bar placement: centerEnd, first item, right after omarchy.clock (the manifest's defaultSection is right)
Panel content width
Panel content height: the content's implicit height, capped at 680 including the card's vertical inset. About 483 with 5 rows in list mode; 52+14+378=444 in globe mode

The content is a non-interactive Flickable that only the wheel scrolls (rows own drags). It extends 12px past the content's right edge so circular buttons can overhang. A wheel notch scrolls 40px, or by pixelDelta. Programmatic scrolls animate over 160ms OutCubic
items.expr: anchors.rightMargin: -Style.space(12); interactive: false; d = pixelDelta.y || angleDelta.y / 120 * Style.space(40)

items.what: Content column: width = contentWidth (scroller.width - 12), spacing panelGap
Dim ink, used for captions, secondary text and the hero caption
items.expr: readonly property color dim: Qt.darker(foreground, 1.55)  // foreground = bar.foreground

items.what: Fainter ink, used for abbreviations, separators and zone ids
Literal gold for the sun marker, globe day dots and terminator (not a theme key)

Widget settings and their defaults. hour24 unset follows the locale's time format (en_US gives 12h). units blank follows the locale (only ImperialUS gives F). offsetMode is home. globeEnabled and smoothMotion are true

Default cities. shell.json stores no cities. The first probe seeds the local city plus 4 SEED_CANDIDATES spread round the dial. Candidates are taken best rank first and must be at least 180 min from home and from each other (relaxed to 120, then 60). They are sorted by hours east of home and persisted as `cities`
items.value: New York, London, Dubai, Tokyo, Los Angeles (worked by hand for local zone America/New_York on 2026-11-02)
items.expr: Model.seedZones({ label: hereZone.label, id: localZone }, offs, 4)

items.what: Fallback list when the local zone is unknown

Offsets come from a `date` probe: one line per zone, "Asia/Tokyo|JST|+0900", plus LOCAL|<zone> from timedatectl. It runs on open and every 5 min; clocks tick every 1 s while open; weather refreshes every 15 min
Hero caption text: local time and home city, plus the scrub delta after two spaces while scrubbed. No full stop
items.value: It's 12:00 PM here in New York

items.what: Caption before the home city is known, and while scrubbed
items.value: "It's 12:00 PM here"; scrubbed: "It's 3:00 PM here in New York  +3h"

items.what: Caption typography: caption 10px on an arc. Each glyph is its own Text, rotated along a circle whose ends drop `rise`. RTL and complex scripts are set flat. Height is about 6+13=19px
items.expr: ArcText { rise: Style.space(6); pixelSize: Style.font.caption; color: hero.captionColor }

items.what: Caption colour: accent while scrubbed, else dim
Caption click, with a pointing cursor while clickable. A picked city sends focus back to home. Otherwise in list mode it toggles the 'Where are you?' search
items.expr: captionClickable: root.focusIndex >= 0 || (root.localZone !== "" && !root.globeMode); onCaptionClicked: focusOn(-1) | hereSearch.stop() | startChoosingHere()

items.what: Title row, centred, spacing 9: "World" [globe] "Clock", title 14px DemiBold, foreground. The column has 2px spacing under the caption
items.expr: Row { spacing: Style.space(9); TitleWord { text: I18n.t("elsewhen.world") } ... TitleWord { text: I18n.t("elsewhen.clock") } }; TitleWord: font.pixelSize: Style.font.title; font.weight: Font.DemiBold

items.what: Mini globe box: round(display 24 * 1.3), rotated by the axial tilt
Click the mini globe to toggle globe mode; Shift+click runs it at 1/3 speed. The pointer hovering it preloads the big globe
items.expr: onClicked: hero.globeClicked((mouse.modifiers & Qt.ShiftModifier) !== 0); onGlobeClicked: root.setGlobeMode(!root.globeMode, slow)

items.what: In globe mode a × (U+00D7) replaces the mini globe. It is round(31*0.8)=25px, dim (foreground on hover), kept upright, opacity clamp((zoom-0.2)/0.35). The mini globe fades as 1 - bigGlobeOpacity

On open the mini globe spins 3 turns and lands on the focus longitude (home): 1250ms OutQuart. If home's coordinates are unknown it waits up to 1500ms, then spins anyway. Picking a city turns the shortest way: 700ms OutCubic
items.expr: globeSpin.from = lon - 1080; globeSpin.to = lon; focusSpin.to = from + Solar.shortestTurn(from, lon)

items.what: Mini globe canvas, r = 31/2-1 = 14.5. Ocean is popups.background mixed 0.16 toward foreground. Graticule (meridians -90 and 0, plus the equator): width max(1, r*0.055)=1, foreground alpha 0.42. Land: rings with 40 or more numbers, foreground alpha 1.0. Rim: width max(1, r*0.095)=1.38, foreground alpha 1.0
items.expr: Model.mix(popups.background, c, bold ? 0.16 : 0.13); Util.alpha(c, showLand ? (bold ? 0.42 : 0.30) : 0.85); lineWidth: Math.max(1, r * (bold ? 0.095 : 0.08))

items.what: 'You are here' marker at the focused city (home by default), on the near side only. Accent dot of r max(1.6, r*0.13)=1.9, edged 1px in background alpha 0.5. Halo ring of r*1.9 (about 3.6), width 1, accent alpha 0.65
items.expr: var mr = Math.max(1.6, r * 0.13); ctx.fillStyle = root.markerColor  // Commons.Color.accent

items.what: Row height: (pad 15 - capGap) + labels + stripGap 9 + track 3 + pad 15. capGap is the space above the capital M in the 13px font (about 4 for JetBrains Mono). Labels are about 17 + 2 + 13. So about 70px, or about 87 with a people line
items.expr: implicitHeight: (pad - panel.capGap) + rowLabels.implicitHeight + stripGap + strip.trackHeight + pad

items.what: Vertical gap between rows

Opaque row fill, popups.background mixed toward foreground. Day 0.10, dawn/dusk 0.07, night 0.035; hover adds 0.05; the picked row gets 0.15. Phase by hour: night <6 or >=20, dawn 6-7, day 8-16, dusk 17-19
items.expr: color: Model.mix(Commons.Color.popups.background, foreground, picked ? dayFill + hoverLift : rowHover.hovered ? phaseFill + hoverLift : phaseFill)

items.what: Row corner radius
Label column: left inset rowPaddingX 12, right edge 10 before the time column, top inset pad - capGap, line spacing 2
items.expr: anchors.leftMargin: Style.spacing.rowPaddingX; anchors.rightMargin: Style.spacing.xl; anchors.topMargin: row.pad - row.panel.capGap; spacing: Style.space(2)

items.what: City name: subtitle 13px DemiBold, foreground, elided right, capped at its natural width + 2. Name line spacing 7; a filler pushes the weather right
items.expr: font.pixelSize: Style.font.subtitle; font.weight: Font.DemiBold; elide: Text.ElideRight; RowLayout { spacing: Style.space(7) }

items.what: Temperature: caption 10px, dim (foreground on hover), pointing cursor. Click flips C/F for the whole list. Hidden until weather arrives. Format is rounded with a unit, e.g. "46°F" or "8°C"
items.expr: text: Model.tempLabel(facts[factsKey(rowData)], units, words); color: tempHover.hovered ? row.foreground : row.dim; onTapped: toggleUnits()

items.what: Weather glyph, bodySmall 11px, dim, from the WMO code. Sunny U+F05A8 (codes 0-1), partly U+F0595 (2), cloudy U+F0590 (3, 45, 48), rain U+F0597 (51-67, 80-82, 95-99), snow U+F0598 (71-77, 85-86). Hidden otherwise
items.expr: weatherGlyph(zone): "\udb81\udda8" sunny, "\udb81\udd95" partly, "\udb81\udd90" cloudy, "\udb81\udd97" rain, "\udb81\udd98" snow

items.what: Weather and coordinates come from Open-Meteo (geocoder, then forecast current temperature_2m and weather_code), with a 20 min TTL. Offline, coordinates fall back to zone1970.tab
People line, shown when the city has people. Up to 4 avatars of round(10*1.45)=15px, overlapping by round(10*0.3)=3px. Then names (caption 10, dim, elided). A GitHub handle shows the profile name
items.expr: spacing: -Math.round(peopleNames.font.pixelSize * 0.3); size: Math.round(peopleNames.font.pixelSize * 1.45); RowLayout { spacing: Style.space(6) }

items.what: Avatar: a GitHub picture masked to a circle, or else the initial (round(15*0.55)=8px DemiBold, foreground) on a disc of row fill mixed 0.28 toward foreground. Edged by max(1, round(size/12))=1px in the row's own fill
items.expr: color: Model.mix(avatar.ground, avatar.foreground, 0.28); font.pixelSize: Math.round(avatar.size * 0.55); anchors.margins: -avatar.edge

items.what: People editor, replacing the people line: TextField with verticalPadding 3 and caption 10px font. Placeholder "Names or @github handles, comma separated". Return or blur keeps the text, Escape cancels. At most 12 people
items.expr: TextField { verticalPadding: Style.space(3); font.pixelSize: Style.font.caption; placeholderText: I18n.t("elsewhen.peoplePlaceholder") }

items.what: Date line, caption 10px, spacing sm 4. Shows the date (ddd MMM d), then '·' (U+00B7, fainter) and the day label when the day differs. The date is dim when a day label shows, else fainter; the day label is dim. Before the probe it shows '…' (U+2026) in fainter
items.expr: text: row.ready ? row.rowData.date : "\u2026"; color: row.ready && row.rowData.dayLabel !== "" ? row.dim : row.fainter; "elsewhen.dateFormat": "ddd MMM d"

items.what: Day label strings: "Tomorrow", "Yesterday", "+2 days" or "-2 days" ("+1 day" form for one); empty on the same day

While hovered, the date crossfades over 110ms to a local greeting for that zone's country language at the city's hour: text in foreground, then a romanisation in fainter (non-Latin only), spacing 5. Examples: New York at 12 shows "Good afternoon"; Tokyo at 2 shows "おやすみ oyasumi"; Dubai at 21 shows "مساء الخير masaa al-khayr"
items.expr: Greet.greeting(rowData.id, ready ? rowData.hour : 0); Row { spacing: Style.space(5) }

items.what: Time column: right inset 12, vertically centred on the labels, spacing 1. Width is the widest '00:00' at 16px DemiBold, plus 3 + the AM/PM width in 12h mode (about 48+3+12=63)
items.expr: width: Math.max(row.panel.timeColumnWidth, implicitWidth); timeColumnWidth: Math.ceil(widestTimeMetrics.advanceWidth + (hour24 ? 0 : Style.spacing.xs + meridiemMetrics.advanceWidth))

items.what: Time: heading 16px DemiBold, foreground; "--:--" before ready. 12h is "h:mm" (no pad), 24h is "HH:mm". The meridiem is a caption on the same baseline, 3px right, dim (foreground on hover). Clicking the time flips 12/24h for the list
items.expr: text: row.ready ? row.rowData.time : "--:--"; font.pixelSize: Style.font.heading; LinkRow { spacing: Style.spacing.xs; onClicked: toggleHour24() }

items.what: Offset line (shown when ready), spacing 5, caption 10px. The %Z zone abbreviation is fainter (dim on hover). Then the offset, fainter (foreground on hover). In home mode it is the distance from local, like "+14h", "-3h" or "+5.5h", and empty on the home offset. In utc mode it reads like "UTC+9", "UTC-5", "UTC+5:30" or "UTC". Clicking it flips the mode
items.expr: Caption { text: rowData.abbr }; Caption { text: row.panel.offsetTextFor(row.rowData) }; onClicked: toggleOffsetMode()

items.what: The row's Caption component: caption 10px, dim by default, PlainText
items.expr: component Caption: Text { color: row.dim; font.pixelSize: Style.font.caption }

items.what: Remove button: PanelActionButton, a 20.35px circle centred on the row's top-right corner, 4.6px in. Glyph × U+00D7, fontSize bodySmall 11, ink dim (foreground on hover), tooltip "Remove". Fill is popups.background mixed toward foreground 0.14 (0.24 hot); the 1px border mixes 0.35 (0.65 hot). It shows on row hover and fades over 120ms. Hidden and disabled on the last city

Who's-here button: the same circle placed 25.35px left of × (or in the corner when there is no ×). Glyph U+F0014 (account-plus), fontSize caption 10, tooltip "Who's here". It shows on hover and hides while editing

Row body, from the top down to the strip: an open-hand cursor. A click picks the city (focusOn), which turns the mini globe and lifts the fill. A vertical drag of 4px or more reorders: the dragged row has opacity 0.9 and z 2, the others ease aside over 130ms OutCubic, and the drop glides 150ms and then persists
items.expr: if (Math.abs(dy) < Style.space(4)) return; armed = true; row.panel.beginRowDrag(row.index, row.height + row.parent.spacing)

items.what: Daylight strip: an 18px-tall hit area inset 12 left and right, centred 16.5px above the row bottom. The track is max(2, 3)=3px high, radius 1.5, foreground alpha 0.10
items.expr: trackHeight: Math.max(2, Style.space(3)); height: Style.space(18); color: Util.alpha(strip.foreground, 0.10); anchors.verticalCenterOffset: -(row.pad + trackHeight / 2)

items.what: Lit spans: foreground alpha 0.28 from that day's computed sunrise to sunset (horizon -0.833deg), the day drawn either side too. Without coordinates it uses a fixed 06:00-18:00. Midnight sun is the full bar; polar night has none. Mirrored for RTL
items.expr: model: strip.sun ? Sun.litSpans(strip.sun) : [{ x0: Model.daylightStart(), x1: Model.daylightEnd() }]; color: Util.alpha(strip.foreground, 0.28)

tray.layout: Bar strip: pinned app icons (27px cells, 12x12 image) against the tray's fixed edge, then the 27px chevron U+F053, with the drawer of unpinned icons sliding open between them on hover (bar.json covers the strip). Left click on an app icon activates it (or opens its menu if the item is menu-only), middle click secondary-activates, right press opens the item's menu card, wheel scrolls the item. Right click on the chevron toggles the 'Tray icons' manage card; left click on the chevron does nothing. TRAY MENU CARD (PopupCard at Tray.qml:573, anchored under the clicked icon): outer width 232px, flat 2px border bar.text at alpha 0.45, padding 8, background popups.background, so the row area is 212px wide. Rows top to bottom are the app's DBus menu entries: item rows 30px tall, separators 11px tall (1px line inset 10px each side, popups.border at 0.45 opacity). An item row: 22px check column at x=0 (U+F00C when checked, only on checkable/radio entries), optional 16x16 icon at x=24, label at x=46 with icon or x=28 without, bodySmall 11px bar.text, elided before a submenu chevron U+203A 10px from the right edge. Hover fills the row with bar.text at alpha 0.08, radius 2; disabled rows at opacity 0.45 and inert. A first root entry that repeats the app title and has children is hidden, as are separators at index 0-1 of the root. Clicking a parent entry drills in: a pinned header appears, a 30px back row (U+2039 in the 22px column, the submenu title at x=28, 11px) plus an 11px separator, and the rows scroll under it. Clicking a leaf triggers it and closes the card. Total outer height = header + rows + 20, capped at 420px, beyond which the rows scroll with an as-needed scrollbar. MANAGE CARD (PopupCard at Tray.qml:447, anchored on the tray): outer width 300px, default PopupCard padding 14 and popups.border, inner 268px. Column with 8px spacing: 'Tray icons' (body 12px bold, bar.text); help text (caption 10px, Qt.darker(bar.text, 1.4), wraps to 2 lines at 268px); 'No tray items reporting.' (bodySmall 11px italic, Qt.darker(bar.text, 1.5)) only when empty; then one 28px row per non-passive item: 16x16 icon at left, name at x=26 (bodySmall 11px, bar.text, elided), and on the right a Hide/Show Button (U+F06E) then 6px then a Pin/Unpin Button (U+F08D), both 11px with 8/3 padding. Typical height with one item is about 118px outer (estimate from font metrics).

wifiqr.layout: Not a bar widget and not a KeyboardPanel: a full-screen OverlayWindow (layer namespace omarchy-network-qr) with no card. A fixed near-black scrim rgba(0,0,0,0.78) covers the output; clicking it dismisses. Centred on screen is a ColumnLayout with 16px spacing (hidden rows take no space), scaled down uniformly only if it would come within 16px of an output edge. Top to bottom: (1) the SSID, uppercased (fallback "WI-FI"), monospace 10 bold, letter-spacing 2, white at alpha 0.55, centred, elided at 320px. (2) The QR code: a white square, radius Style.cornerRadius (0), each dark module a #111111 square of moduleSize = max(4, floor(240 / qrSize)) px; the matrix already carries a 4-module white quiet zone. A typical WPA payload gives a 37-module matrix (29 + 2x4), so modules are 6px and the square is 222px. (3) While generating, "Generating QR code…" in monospace 11, white 0.55, centred, and the QR is hidden. (4) On failure, the error (stderr of omarchy-network-qr, else "Could not generate the Wi-Fi QR code") in monospace 11, #ff6b6b, wrapping at 320px. (5) Under a shown code, "Scan to join this network" in monospace 11, white 0.55. (6) Only for a secured network, a clickable line (pointing-hand cursor) "Show password" in monospace 11 white at opacity 0.6. Clicking it runs omarchy-network-password and replaces it with the password itself at opacity 1, wrapping anywhere at 320px. Clicking again hides it. A failed lookup shows "Could not read the Wi-Fi password" in #ff6b6b. Colours are fixed, not themed. Esc dismisses. There are no other keys and no tooltips.

speedtest.layout: Not a bar widget. The network speed test summons the shared SpeedTestOverlay (shell/Ui/SpeedTestOverlay.qml), a full-screen PanelWindow on the Overlay layer (namespace omarchy-network-speedtest, exclusive keyboard, ignores exclusive zones, anchored to all edges) with no card. A fixed scrim rgba(0,0,0,0.78) covers the output; clicking it closes. Centred is a ColumnLayout with 16px spacing, shrink-to-fit with 16px clearance. Top to bottom: (1) the title, the connection name uppercased (SSID, or the translated Ethernet), monospace 10 bold, letter-spacing 2, white 0.55, centred, hidden when empty. (2) A row of two 210x210 dials with 48px between them (468px total): DOWNLOAD on the left, UPLOAD on the right. Each dial has an open 270-degree arc, starting at 135 degrees (bottom-left, clockwise) with its 90-degree gap at the bottom. The arc stroke is 4px with round caps, at radius 101. The track is white 0.14. The value arc is in Color.accent with a 12px under-glow at accent alpha 0.18. Inside the arc is a tick ring of 46 ticks; every 5th is major (2x10px, white 0.30, top at 8px); minors are 1x6px, white 0.12, top at 10px. The needle is a hubless 3px-wide sliver, 67.2px long, starting 18px in from the rim and fading from accent to transparent toward the centre. The readout sits 14px below centre: the number in monospace 24 bold white (1 decimal under 10, else 0), and under it the unit "Mbps" in monospace 10, white 0.55. The dial label sits at the bottom inside the gap, in monospace 10 bold, letter-spacing 1.5, white 0.55. A dial that is not live and reads 0 sits at opacity 0.5. (3) A bordered "Run Again" Button, centred, monospace 11, white foreground, padding 14x4. It fades to opacity 0 (keeping its space) while a run is in flight. Tooltip: "Measure again via speed.omarchy.org". (4) The error in monospace 11, #ff6b6b, wrapping at 440px, shown only on failure. On open, both needles sweep to full scale over 550ms and back over 650ms, then track live readings with a 600ms glide. The full scale latches upward through 100/250/500/1000/2500/5000/10000 Mbps, shared by both dials. Esc or a scrim click closes. Enter or Return runs again when idle.
